title: TracePoint result
description: The system of record for one run. Every other output - the terminal tables, the HTML report, the Markdown summary, the JUnit file and the agent digest - is a pure function of this document, so anything absent here cannot be shown anywhere. Latency is reported two ways throughout: response_time is measured from the scheduled send time and is what a user feels, service_time is measured from the moment a connection was in hand and is what the target actually did. SLOs are judged on response time; tier attribution uses service time.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's shape, MAJOR.MINOR. A reader written against 1.x must ignore unknown fields; a MAJOR bump means a migration is required. Tools that cannot migrate exit 3.

tool.description: The binary that produced this document.

version.description: Release version, or dev for local builds.

go.description: Go toolchain the binary was built with.

config.description: The configuration that actually ran, after interpolation, defaults, overrides and policy clamping - with every secret redacted. Kept here so the result is self-sufficient: compare can diff two runs' settings, and `run --from` can reproduce one, without the original file.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of effective, prefixed with the algorithm.

effective.description: The redacted effective configuration, conforming to config.schema.json.

source_path.description: Where the configuration was read from, or - for stdin.

policy.description: The policy in force, conforming to policy.schema.json.

runners.description: One entry per runner that took part, in configuration order. App runners carry the traffic whose latency users feel; storage runners are simultaneously load and probe.

capacity.description: Present only for capacity searches. Null or absent for an ordinary run.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices raised anywhere during the run, in the order they occurred.

artifacts.description: Where the run's files live, as paths relative to the run directory unless absolute.

raw.description: The optional per-operation raw sink, when --raw was used.

run.description: Identity and timing of the run. All offsets in this document are milliseconds from the single monotonic start shared by every runner and sampler; wall-clock times are for display only.

id.description: Run identifier: a UTC timestamp and a short random suffix. Also the run directory name.

started_at.description: Wall-clock start of load, after preflight.

status.description: How the run ended. completed ran to plan; interrupted was stopped by a signal or stop request and holds partial data; aborted was cut short by the abort guard; failed could not produce usable data.

elapsed_ms.description: Actual load duration. Shorter than duration_ms when the run was interrupted or aborted.

bucket_ms.description: Bucket width. Every runner and sampler shares it.

bucket_count.description: Number of buckets the timeline spans.

warmup_ms.description: Leading period excluded from every summary, baseline and SLO check.

min_samples.description: Below this many operations a bucket is insufficient and is never used as evidence.

seed.description: Seed actually used. Reusing it reproduces every random choice.

arrival.description: Arrival process used by open-model executors.

interrupted_reason.description: Why a run ended early, when it did.

host.description: The generator machine, for judging whether the generator could have been the bottleneck.

open_file_limit.description: Soft RLIMIT_NOFILE, which caps concurrent connections.

quantiles.description: A latency distribution in milliseconds, read from a merged sketch with 1% relative accuracy. Quantiles are never averaged across buckets; they are always recomputed from merged sketches.

p999.description: 99.9th percentile. Unreliable below a few thousand samples.

errorCounts.description: Failures by class. Classes are fixed: adding one is a minor version change, so readers must tolerate unknown keys. A class absent from the object means zero.

connection.description: Refused, reset or closed before a response.

pool_timeout.description: No connection became free within the deadline. A generator-side limit, not a target failure.

http_4xx.description: A 4xx status outside the expected set. Does not count towards the abort guard.

http_5xx.description: A 5xx status outside the expected set.

expect_failed.description: The response arrived but failed a status or JSON expectation.

extract_failed.description: A value a later step needed could not be extracted, so the iteration stopped.

query_error.description: The database or Redis server returned an error.

canceled.description: The operation was cut short by shutdown, not by the target.

sketch.description: A serialised relative-error sketch for the whole run, kept so compare can compute order-statistic confidence intervals on quantiles without the raw observations.

relative_accuracy.description: Guaranteed relative error of any quantile read from it.

count.description: Number of observations, needed for confidence intervals.

opSummary.description: Aggregate statistics over the measured window - the whole run excluding warm-up - for one runner or one label.

ok.description: Operations that succeeded and met every expectation.

response_ms.description: Response time: end minus the scheduled send time. Coordinated-omission corrected, and what SLOs are judged on.

service_ms.description: Service time: end minus the moment a connection was in hand. What the target did, and what tier attribution uses.

client_wait_ms.description: Time lost inside the generator: dispatch lag plus queue wait plus pool wait. When this dominates, the finding is about the generator, not the target.

achieved_rps.description: Completed operations per second over the measured window.

bytes_in.description: Response bytes read. Bodies are drained and discarded, never stored.

bucket.description: One sealed time bucket for one runner. Sealing happens once no in-flight operation can still land in it, after which the bucket is a fixed-size summary and its sketch is freed - which is why memory does not grow with run length.

i.description: Bucket index from the run start.

t_ms.description: Offset of the bucket's start from the run start.

n.description: Operations whose scheduled time fell in this bucket and which completed.

insufficient.description: True when n is below run.min_samples. Such buckets are drawn in charts but never used as evidence for a hot bucket, an incident or a verdict.

warmup.description: True when the bucket falls inside warm-up and is therefore excluded from summaries and baselines.

rps.description: Completed operations per second in this bucket.

offered.description: Arrivals scheduled in this bucket, whether or not they were dispatched.

dropped.description: Arrivals refused because every worker was busy and the dispatch queue was full. Never silently delayed.

in_flight_max.description: Peak concurrent operations during the bucket. The x-axis of the strain finder and of Little's Law checks.

bytes_in.description: Response bytes read in this bucket.

runner.description: Everything recorded for one runner. Storage runners double as probes: because they hit the datastore directly, their per-bucket latency is a health signal for that tier under the combined pressure of application traffic and this synthetic traffic.

name.description: Runner name: http, db or redis.

kind.description: app for the tier users talk to, storage for a probe-and-load tier behind it.

driver.description: For db, the driver in use.

targets.description: Resolved targets, for the same-host caveat and the safety record. Credentials are redacted.

addrs.description: Addresses it resolved to at preflight.

scope.description: Address classification driving the policy decision and the same-host caveat.

labels.description: Labels seen, capped at 50 per runner; the overflow is collected under 'other'. Labels are request, step, query or command names - never raw URLs.

executor.description: What the executor actually did, as opposed to what was asked for. The gap between offered and dispatched is the first thing to check when a run is suspicious.

dropped.description: Arrivals refused for want of a worker. Above 1% this is reported, and it changes what the run can prove.

peak_in_flight.description: Highest concurrency actually reached. Equal to max_in_flight means the ceiling bound the run.

dispatch_lag_ms.description: How late arrivals were handed out relative to their scheduled time. A p99 above max(5ms, 5% of a bucket) means the generator itself fell behind and the run is invalid.

sketches.description: Merged whole-run sketches for significance testing in compare. The key __runner__ holds the runner-wide sketch; other keys are labels.

buckets.description: The sealed timeline, in index order.

label_buckets.description: Per-label timelines, keyed by label. Retained only while labels x buckets stays within the retention budget (see docs/adr/002); beyond it only the per-runner timeline above is kept, whole-run per-label statistics survive in labels_summary and sketches, and a LABEL_TIMELINE_DROPPED warning is recorded. Analysis never depends on this field.

status_histogram.description: Counts by status code, as strings. Used to detect a run that is measuring a rate limiter rather than a service.

phases_ms.description: Where the time went inside a request, from httptrace.

conn_wait.description: Waiting for a connection from the client pool. Generator-side.

ttfb.description: First byte after the request was written: the target's think time.

conn_reuse_ratio.description: Share of requests served on a reused connection. A low value with keep-alive on usually means an undersized idle pool.

insecure_tls.description: Whether certificate verification was disabled. Printed in every report when true.

pool.description: Pool behaviour from database/sql. Waiting here is generator-side, not database latency, which is why connections are acquired explicitly and timed apart from the query.

peak_in_use.description: Highest number of connections simultaneously checked out.

wait_count.description: How many times a caller had to wait for a connection.

wait_ms_total.description: Total time spent waiting for connections.

pool.description: go-redis pool statistics. A timeout or a wait here is generator-side.

misses.description: Times a new connection had to be made.

telemetry.description: Server-side and generator-side health sampled on the same offset clock as the load, so a spike can be lined up against what the datastore was doing. Every sampler is read-only and fails soft: when a permission is missing the sampler reports available: false with a reason instead of failing the run, and the verdict's confidence drops accordingly.

generator.description: Self-health of the load generator, always collected. This is what distinguishes 'the target is slow' from 'we could not ask fast enough'.

cpu_ratio.description: Process CPU use as a fraction of one core times GOMAXPROCS.

heap_bytes.description: Heap in use. Flat across a soak run is the acceptance criterion.

sched_latency_p99_ms.description: 99th percentile goroutine scheduling delay. Rising here means the generator is saturated.

dispatch_lag_p99_ms.description: Per runner, how late arrivals were dispatched.

in_flight.description: Per runner, operations in flight at the sample.

samplerSeries.description: One datastore sampler's output. Counter-style metrics are stored as deltas between samples, not as raw totals, so they can be read directly.

available.description: False when the sampler could not run - usually a missing grant. The reason is given, and verdicts fall back to latency evidence alone.

reason.description: Why it was unavailable, in plain words.
examples: permission denied for pg_stat_activity; grant pg_read_all_stats

samples.description: Samples in time order. Keys vary by sampler and are documented in docs/METHODOLOGY.md; readers must tolerate unknown keys.

statements.description: Postgres only: an end-of-run top-N from pg_stat_statements, when enabled. Query text is normalised by the server and never carries literal values.

finding.description: A coded observation. Findings never carry free-form target output: strings taken from a target are truncated, stripped of control characters and labelled.

code.description: Stable identifier from the registry in docs/ERRORS.md.

severity.description: info is context, warn degrades the run, error invalidates it.

message.description: One sentence a human can act on.

analysis.description: Everything derived from the recorded data. Each field is produced by a pure function of the runners and telemetry above, so the same result always yields the same analysis.

validity.description: Whether this run can be believed at all. Read it before anything else: an invalid run measured the generator, not the target, and its verdict must not be interpreted.

state.description: valid means the generator kept up and nothing undermines the numbers. degraded means they are usable with a stated caveat. invalid means the generator, not the target, set the pace - the run proves nothing about the target and the CLI exits 4 unless --allow-invalid.

findings.description: Why it is not valid, if it is not.

slo.description: Budget evaluation on response time over the measured window. A breach makes the run exit 1.

pass.description: True when every check passed. Absent budgets are not checks.

budget.description: The configured limit: milliseconds for latency, a ratio for error_rate.

actual.description: The measured value in the same unit.

thresholds.description: The hot-bucket threshold each runner was judged against, and where it came from: an SLO, a flag, or the 100ms default.

hot_buckets.description: Per runner, the buckets judged abnormal, with the rule that fired. absolute means p99 service time exceeded the threshold. relative means the bucket stood out against a rolling median of the previous 30 steady buckets by all three of: a modified z-score above 3.5, at least three times the median, and at least 5ms above it. Insufficient buckets are never hot.

baseline_ms.description: Rolling median it was compared against.

mz_score.description: Modified z-score against that rolling window.

incidents.description: Hot buckets merged into episodes and classified. This, not a list of spikes, is what a reader should look at.

correlation.description: Whole-run Spearman rank correlation between the application p99 series and each storage probe's p99 series, evaluated at lags of minus three to plus three buckets. A positive best lag means the storage tier moved first, which is what one expects when the storage tier is the cause.

storage.description: Storage runner compared against the app.

rho.description: Spearman rho at the best lag, from -1 to 1.

best_lag_buckets.description: Lag maximising |rho|. Positive means storage led the app.

rho_by_lag.description: Rho at every lag tried, keyed by lag.

n_buckets.description: Buckets that were sufficient in both series. Below about 30 the correlation is weak evidence.

lean.description: Which way the evidence points on this pair alone.

verdict.description: The answer to the question the tool exists for. Deterministic: the same result always produces the same words. It always states that correlation is not proof.

bottleneck.description: Where the latency came from. app means the application tier itself; db or redis names a storage tier; client means the generator or its configuration, not the target; none means nothing stood out; inconclusive means the data cannot say.

confidence.description: How much weight to put on it, from sample sizes, the number of incidents, the strength of the correlation and whether telemetry corroborated it.

summary.description: One paragraph in plain words, safe to quote verbatim.

evidence.description: The specific observations behind the verdict, each independently checkable in this document.

kind.description: What sort of evidence this is.

caveat.description: The standing limitation of the method: shared timing shows association, not causation.

next_steps.description: What to do next, concretely and in priority order.

strain.description: For ramping runs, the load level at which latency started to degrade: the first run of at least three consecutive sufficient buckets where application p99 exceeded twice the median of the early steady buckets.

found.description: Whether strain was observed within the range tested.

users.description: Concurrent operations in flight at that point.

baseline_p99_ms.description: Early steady median the threshold was built from.

message.description: The finding in one sentence, such as 'strain begins at ~180 users (~420 req/s)'.

next_window.description: The load range a follow-up capacity search should cover.

incident.description: A contiguous episode of abnormal latency, formed by merging a runner's hot buckets across gaps of one bucket and then overlapping runners with a tolerance of one bucket either side. The class is the finding: it says which tier the episode implicates.

class.description: correlated: the application and at least one storage tier were hot together - the storage tier is a candidate cause. storage_only: a storage tier was hot while the application stayed within budget, a bottleneck that has not yet reached users. app_only: the application was hot while every storage probe was healthy on sufficient data, which points at the application tier. client_limited: the generator's own waiting dominated, so the target is not implicated. unobserved: the application was hot but the storage probes had too little data to say anything.

runners.description: Every runner's behaviour during the window, hot or not. A runner that stayed healthy is as much a part of the finding as one that did not.

hot.description: Whether this runner was hot in the window.

first_hot_i.description: First bucket at which it went hot, the basis of lead time.

peak_p99_ms.description: Highest service-time p99 in the window.

severity.description: Peak p99 divided by this runner's threshold.

insufficient.description: True when this runner had too little data in the window to judge.

culprit.description: The best-ranked storage tier inside a correlated incident, by lead time, severity and telemetry corroboration. Null when no tier stands out, and ties are reported rather than broken arbitrarily.

score.description: Ranking score; comparable only within this incident.

lead_buckets.description: How many buckets it went hot before the application did.

tied_with.description: Runners that scored equally. When non-empty the incident does not name a single cause.

app_impact.description: What users would have felt during the window.

peak_p99_ms.description: Worst application p99 in the window.

slo_breached.description: Whether the application budget was exceeded.

affected_ops.description: Application operations that fell inside the window.

telemetry.description: Server-side signals that moved in the same window, which is what raises a correlation to corroborated evidence.

note.description: What it means in one sentence.

confidence.description: How much weight this single incident carries.

capacity.description: The result of an auto-ramp search: levels are doubled until one breaks, then the boundary is refined and re-run to confirm it is stable.

phase.description: Which part of the search produced it.

ok.description: Whether it held every SLO and kept up with the offered load.

break_reason.description: Why it broke: an SLO breach, or throughput plateauing below 90% of what was offered.

mean_concurrency.description: Measured mean in-flight operations, the x value of the USL fit.

culprit.description: Which tier broke this level, by the same analysis a whole run uses.

boundary.description: Where capacity ran out. Confirmed by re-running both sides once: if either flips, a range is reported instead of a point, because a boundary that moves between runs is not a number worth quoting.

range.description: When unstable, the range the true boundary lies in.

knee.description: Load at which latency began climbing sharply, when one is identifiable.

usl.description: Universal Scalability Law fit over the levels that held: X(N) = lambda*N / (1 + sigma*(N-1) + kappa*N*(N-1)). Sigma is contention, kappa is crosstalk. The fit is hidden when R-squared is below 0.9 or fewer than four levels held, because an unreliable extrapolation is worse than none.

fitted.description: Whether a fit is being reported.

reason.description: Why it is not, when it is not.

lambda.description: Ideal throughput per unit of concurrency.

sigma.description: Contention coefficient: the serialised share of the work.

kappa.description: Crosstalk coefficient: coherency cost, which makes throughput fall back after the peak.

r2.description: Coefficient of determination of the fit.

peak_n.description: Concurrency of predicted peak throughput, sqrt((1-sigma)/kappa).
